from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Hook & Prerequisite Knowledge", [

            "It travels fastest in a vacuum.",
            "Changing speed changes direction."

        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW), run_time=1)

    def construct(self):

        self.setup_layout("Defining Refraction & Snell's Law", lecture_lines)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Bending Rule", ["Denser medium, light bends inward.", "Rarer medium, light bends outward.", "The normal line is our reference."])
        
        # Mobjects
        normal_line = Line(start=self.grid['A4'], end=self.grid['F4'], color=GRAY)
        interface = Line(start=self.grid['C1'], end=self.grid['C6'], color=BLUE_B)

        r_ray_denser = Line(start=self.grid['C4'], end=self.grid['E5'], color=YELLOW)
        
        snells_law = MathTex(r"n_1 \sin(i) = n_2 \sin(r)", font_size=32, color=GOLD)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.title))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.add(normal_line, interface)
        self.play(Create(i_ray), Create(r_ray_denser))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Quick Check", ["Speed changes cause refraction.", "Light bends at interfaces.", "Straws look broken underwater."])
        
        # Define elements
        straw = Line(start=UP*1.5, end=DOWN*1.5, color="#FFD700", stroke_width=8)
        water_line = Line(start=LEFT*2, end=RIGHT*2, color="#00BFFF", stroke_width=4)

        straw_top = Line(start=UP*1.5, end=ORIGIN, color="#FFD700", stroke_width=8)

outline.topic: The Physics of Refraction: Why Light Bends

sections.title: Hook & Prerequisite Knowledge
sections.content: Introduce the behavior of light as a wave. Review the concept of 'wave speed' in different media. Explain that light travels at its maximum speed in a vacuum (c).
sections.example: Visualize a row of soldiers marching from a smooth pavement onto thick, muddy grass. As the soldiers hit the mud, they slow down, causing the entire line to pivot (change direction).

sections.title: Defining Refraction & Snell's Law
sections.content: Define refraction as the change in direction of a light wave passing from one medium to another due to a change in speed. Introduce the Refractive Index (n = c/v). Present Snell's Law: n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2).
sections.example: A laser beam hitting a glass prism at an angle. Show an animation where the incoming angle (θ1) is compared to the outgoing angle (θ2) using a protractor overlay.

sections.title: Visualizing the Bending Rule
sections.content: Establish the golden rule: When light enters a denser medium (higher n), it bends toward the normal line. When entering a rarer medium, it bends away from the normal line.
sections.example: An animation of an underwater 'Archerfish' aiming at a beetle on a branch. The fish must account for the light refracting at the water-air interface to hit its target.

sections.title: Real-World Applications
sections.content: Connect the theory to optical devices. Explain how convex lenses rely on refraction to converge light, forming the basis for human vision and high-tech equipment.
sections.example: A camera lens focusing light onto a digital sensor, or a human eye showing how light bends through the cornea and lens to focus an image onto the retina.

sections.title: Summary & Quick Check
sections.content: Recap: Speed change leads to direction change. Final check: What happens to a straw in a glass of water? It looks 'broken' because our brain assumes light travels in straight lines.
sections.example: A 5-second animation of a pencil being inserted into a clear glass of water, illustrating the 'broken' appearance versus the actual path of the submerged portion.
